about.title: Fountain Valley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Fountain Valley's mix of arterial roads and freeway access points, especially where Brookhurst, Euclid, and Edinger feed into I-405, sees a steady share of Orange County traffic. Public records show 60 injury collisions and 87 people hurt in the most recent final year, with reported crashes clustering on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. as commuters and shoppers overlap. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the period right after matters: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness contact information can disappear within days. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect injured Fountain Valley residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and explain options under California law. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward. Our role is to make that first step easier during a stressful time.

whyChoose.title: Why Fountain Valley Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the crash date to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like a city road crew, was involved. An attorney can help you spot that deadline early.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for a crash at a busy Brookhurst or Edinger intersection, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help document your share of fault accurately.

items.title: No Recorded Statement Without Guidance
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly after a crash; that statement can be used against you later. Getting attorney guidance first, on contingency and at no upfront cost, helps protect your position.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Fountain Valley?
items.answer: California's statute of limitations is generally two years from the date of the crash. If a government entity, such as one responsible for road maintenance near I-405 or Edinger, may be involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a statement?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other side's insurer before speaking with an attorney, since those statements can be used to minimize your claim. LawProactive can connect you with someone who can advise you on next steps before you say anything official.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. We are not a law firm and don't charge for the connection itself.
